title: The Gift of the Magi

teacherSummary.text: On Christmas Eve Della Young has only $1.87 to buy a present for her husband Jim. She sells her long, beautiful hair for twenty dollars and buys a platinum fob chain for Jim's prized gold watch. Jim comes home and reveals he has sold the watch to buy Della a set of tortoise-shell combs for her hair. The narrator calls the two foolish children but declares them the wisest of givers: they are the magi.

segments.activity: Model the close reading of the anchor quotation using the written think-aloud below.
segments.script: First, meaning. I read “ONE dollar and eighty-seven cents. That was all” slowly and put it in my own words: The story begins with Della's entire savings: one dollar and eighty-seven cents, the day before Christmas. Next, craft. I notice the exact amount spelled out, followed by "That was all," a short sentence that lands like a sigh. The strongest word is “All”: it stresses that nothing else is coming. Then, effect. What problem does the opening sum create for Della? My answer: The opening sum creates the problem that Della cannot afford a worthy gift for Jim, so it pushes her to sell her hair; the story begins with the poverty that makes both sacrifices necessary.
